evidence: src/application/create-user-use-case.ts: in CreateUserUseCase.execute, `throw new ApplicationError("name is required", 400)` hard-codes HTTP status 400, which is a transport concern that belongs to the infrastructure layer.
The rest of execute is application orchestration: it calls ids.next(), runs new User(...), calls users.save(user) and maps the result to a UserOutput DTO.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: CreateUserUseCase.execute mostly does application-layer work. It validates input, creates the domain User, saves it through the UserRepository port and returns a UserOutput DTO. One statement does not belong here: `throw new ApplicationError("name is required", 400)` puts an HTTP status code in the application layer. Turning a failure into an HTTP status is a transport job, which belongs to the infrastructure layer (UserController / http-server.ts). The use case should report a semantic error, such as a validation error, and let the transport adapter choose the status code. The leak is small, so confidence is moderate.
